facts.value: Infants should be breastfed exclusively during the first 6 months of life.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Infants should be breastfed continuously until 2 years of age and beyond.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: From 6 months of age, breast milk should be complemented with a variety of adequate, safe and nutrient-dense foods. Salt and sugars should not be added to complementary foods.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Infants and young children of 6–23 months of age should consume a diverse diet that includes animal source foods, such as meat, fish, or eggs, as well as fruits and vegetables.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Consumption of starchy staple foods should be minimized.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Foods high in sugar, salt and trans fats as well as sweet beverages should be avoided.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree
